bugs.title: mulligan_rewind granularity 'last_turn' with to_previous_prompt:true silently fails — tool reports success but filter no-ops
bugs.description: When the agent calls mulligan_rewind with granularity:'last_turn' and to_previous_prompt:true in a session with 2+ user messages, the tool computes a non-empty removal set (K>0, including the latest user message), persists the marker + note, and returns a success text claiming 'N messages will be hidden from your view starting next turn.' However, the context filter's protectedOk() unconditionally protects the latest user message (protectLatestUser) and has no awareness of the to_previous_prompt option (it receives only messages/remove/config, not the marker's options). Since the nuclear removal set includes the latest user index, protectedOk returns false, and filterPipeline silently skips the rewind via `continue`. The result: the tool lies to the agent (claims success, K messages hidden) while the filter hides nothing. The spec (PRD §8) explicitly states the latest user is protected 'unless to_previous_prompt explicitly and it isn't the first' — so to_previous_prompt with 2+ users SHOULD be allowed. With only 1 user message the tool correctly refuses (step 5b, K=0), meaning to_previous_prompt NEVER actually works in any scenario: refused with 1 user, silently no-ops with 2+. This violates the PRD's 'honest bookkeeping' design principle (#6) and success criterion #1 (autonomous shedding).
bugs.reproduction: 1. Create a message list with 2+ user messages and tool work after the latest user. 2. Simulate the tool: call filterPipeline with a rewind marker {seq:1, granularity:'last_turn', options:{to_previous_prompt:true}, excludeToolCallId:'rw'} and default config (protectedRoles:['first:user','latest:user']). 3. Observe: the filter returns the input UNCHANGED (length unchanged, 'big2' content still present). 4. Equivalently via the tool: the tool's resolvePreview computes K=3 and returns 'Mulligan: rewound last_turn. 3 messages will be hidden...' but feeding the persisted marker back through filterPipeline yields zero messages hidden. (Verified in probe tests: LIVE path out len 9==9; PIN path with hideEntryIds out len 9==9 — both no-op.)
bugs.expected: Per PRD §6 §4 step 3 and §8: a to_previous_prompt last_turn rewind with 2+ user messages should remove the latest user message and everything after it (except the rewind's own unit + mulligan notes), landing the model at the PREVIOUS user prompt. The filter should apply it, not skip it.
bugs.actual: The filter's protectedOk() blanket-protects the latest user regardless of to_previous_prompt, causing filterPipeline to `continue` (skip) the rewind. The tool has already persisted the marker + note and reported K>0 success. The content remains fully visible to the model. The agent is misled into believing it rewound when it did not.
bugs.location: src/transforms.ts — protectedOk() (protectLatestUser block, ~line 'if (protectLatestUser)') has no exemption for to_previous_prompt. Also src/transforms.ts filterPipeline (~the `if (!protectedOk(...))` block) silently continues for non-checkpoint granularities. The tool src/tools/rewind.ts step 5b only refuses when K===0 (single-user case) and does not catch the 2+-user mismatch.
bugs.suggestedFix: Pass the rewind marker's options (specifically to_previous_prompt) into protectedOk, or relocate the latest-user protection check into resolveLastTurn (which already knows about to_previous_prompt and already enforces iFirstUser!==iLastUser). When granularity is 'last_turn' and options.to_previous_prompt===true, exempt the latest user from protection. The cleanest fix: make protectedOk accept the marker (or a flags object) and skip protectLatestUser when to_previous_prompt is true. Ensure the filterPipeline call site passes this through.

bugs.title: Checkpoint rewind that crosses the latest user message: tool over-reports K and filter partially applies (trims) instead of refusing per spec
bugs.description: When the agent rewinds to a checkpoint that was set BEFORE the latest user message, the removal set (everything after the checkpoint target) includes the latest user. The tool's resolvePreview computes K = full removal count (including the latest user) and reports 'K messages will be hidden.' But the filter's protectedOk blocks the full removal (latest user protected), and filterPipeline has special-case code that TRIMS the removal set for checkpoint granularity (removing only indices < iLatestUser) instead of skipping or refusing. The result: the tool says '5 messages hidden' but the filter only hides 2 (the messages between the checkpoint and the latest user), keeping the latest user and current turn. The agent believes it rewound to the checkpoint but actually lands at a non-contiguous view [checkpoint-area ... latest-user ... current-turn] with the middle content missing. The PRD §6 step 6 says 'Refuse if iTarget falls at/before a protected message' and §8 says a rewind that removes the latest user 'is refused' — the implementation neither refuses (tool) nor no-ops (filter) but partially applies, contradicting both. This creates a tool/filter mismatch where the reported K is wrong.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Messages: [user('task'), asst(c1), tRes(c1), user('middle'), asst(c2), tRes(c2), user('latest ask'), asst(rw), tRes(rw), note]. 2. Branch entries mapping each message to an id, plus a label entry {type:'label', targetId:'e2' (the c1 result), label:'mulligan:checkpoint:cp'}. 3. Run filterPipeline with marker {seq:1, granularity:'checkpoint', checkpoint:'cp', excludeToolCallId:'rw'}. 4. Observe: result length 7 (orig 10) — indices 3,4,5 (middle user + c2 + res) removed, but index 6 (latest ask) and the tail KEPT. The tool would have reported K>=4 (everything after e2). The filter only hid 3. (Verified in probe4 test: 'checkpoint crosses latest: out len 7 orig 10'.)
bugs.expected: Per PRD §6 step 6 and §8: the rewind should be REFUSED (the tool returns a refusal text and creates no marker; the filter no-ops) because the removal would cross the protected latest user message. Alternatively, if partial application is desired, the tool's reported K must match what the filter actually hides.
bugs.actual: The tool persists the marker and reports the FULL K (e.g. 4+ messages hidden). The filter's protectedOk fails, then the checkpoint-specific trimming code removes only the messages before the latest user (3 messages), keeping the latest user and current turn. The agent is told '4 messages hidden' but only 3 are hidden, and the view is non-contiguous (checkpoint content, then latest-user + current turn, with middle content missing).
bugs.location: src/transforms.ts — filterPipeline, the `if (!protectedOk(m, remove, config))` block with the checkpoint-specific `remove = remove.filter((r) => r < iLatestUser)` trimming. Also src/tools/rewind.ts — resolvePreview/step 5b does not check whether a checkpoint removal crosses the latest user before persisting.
bugs.suggestedFix: Either (a) make the tool refuse checkpoint rewinds whose removal set includes the latest user (analogous to step 5b for last_turn), so no marker is persisted and K is never mis-reported; or (b) if the trimming behavior is intentional, make the tool compute K from the TRIMMED removal set so the reported count matches the filter's actual behavior. Option (a) aligns with the spec's 'refuse' semantics.

bugs.title: Sequential last_tool_call_group rewinds mis-target each other on the unpinned (live) fallback path
bugs.description: When two or more last_tool_call_group rewind markers coexist and lack hideEntryIds pins, resolveLastToolCallGroup only excludes the CURRENT marker's own excludeToolCallId — it does not exclude OTHER rewinds' tool-call groups. Applied oldest-first: rewind#1 resolves 'last tool group excluding rewind#1's own call' and finds rewind#2's group (the last group from the end that isn't rewind#1's own); rewind#1 then removes rewind#2's confirmation. Then rewind#2 removes rewind#1's confirmation. The net result is the exact INVERSE of intent: both mistake spans (the bloated grep/read the agent wanted to hide) remain visible, while both rewind confirmations are hidden. The spec §11 composition example explicitly states the correct result should keep both rewind confirmations and shed both mistakes. The implementation mitigates this via a hideEntryIds pin (BUG-002 fix) populated by the rewind tool at creation time, and the normal end-to-end flow (agent calls the tool) populates the pin correctly. However, the pin is absent when (a) resolvePreview throws (e.g. a malformed branch entry causes sessionEntryToContextMessages to throw, since resolvePreview has no per-entry try/catch), (b) the marker was created externally/legacy, or (c) the pin resolves to empty (compaction). In those cases the live fallback silently produces the inverted result with no error.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Messages: [user, asst(grep-c), tRes(grep-c,'BIG-GREP'), asst(read-c), tRes(read-c,'BIG-READ'), asst(rw1), tRes(rw1), note, asst(rw2), tRes(rw2)]. 2. Markers: [{seq:1, granularity:'last_tool_call_group', excludeToolCallId:'rw1'}, {seq:2, granularity:'last_tool_call_group', excludeToolCallId:'rw2'}] (NO hideEntryIds). 3. Run filterPipeline. 4. Observe: result keeps BIG-GREP and BIG-READ (indices 1-4) and removes the rewind confirmations (the rw1/rw2 groups). Output roles: [user, assistant, toolResult, assistant, toolResult, custom] — the exact OPPOSITE of the spec §11 intent. (Verified in probe2 test.) NOTE: with hideEntryIds pins populated, the same fixture produces the CORRECT result (both mistakes hidden) — the existing PIN test at pipeline.test.ts:695 confirms this.
bugs.expected: Per PRD §11: two last_tool_call_group rewinds should compose to hide BOTH mistake spans and keep BOTH rewind confirmations + the note. The filter result should be [user, rw1+res, note, rw2+res]. resolveLastToolCallGroup should exclude ALL mulligan_rewind tool groups, not just the current marker's own.
bugs.actual: On the unpinned live path, rewind#1 targets rewind#2's group and rewind#2 targets rewind#1's group. Both mistakes remain visible; both rewind confirmations are hidden. The agent sees the bloated content it tried to shed and loses its rewind confirmations.
bugs.location: src/transforms.ts — resolveLastToolCallGroup (only excludes excludeToolCallId, not all rewind call ids). The mitigation is the hideEntryIds pin arm in filterPipeline, but the live fallback (`else if (granularity === 'last_tool_call_group')`) uses the broken resolver.
bugs.suggestedFix: In filterPipeline, collect ALL rewind markers' excludeToolCallIds and pass them as a set to resolveLastToolCallGroup (change the exclude param from a single string to a Set/array), so every rewind's own group is skipped when resolving any rewind's target. This makes the live fallback correct without relying solely on the pin.

bugs.title: Two mulligan_shrink markers with by_content_includes on the same target: the second shrink silently no-ops (contradicts PRD E17 'last wins')
bugs.description: PRD edge case E17 states: 'Two shrink markers match the same target → applied in seq order; last wins (its replacement is what's seen).' This holds for stable matchers (by_tool_call_id, by_tool_name) because the toolCallId/toolName survive the first shrink's content substitution. But for by_content_includes, the first shrink REPLACES the matched message's content with the agent's replacement. If the replacement no longer contains the second shrink's needle substring, the second shrink's resolveShrinkTarget returns null on the already-shrunk message and silently no-ops. The 'last wins' guarantee is violated: the FIRST shrink's replacement persists instead of the second's. There is no error or warning. This is an inherent fragility of content-substring matching after substitution, but it contradicts the spec's stated E17 invariant.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Messages: [user, asst(c1), tRes(c1, 'ORIGINAL BIG CONTENT WITH NEEDLE HERE'), asstText('done')]. 2. Shrinks: [{seq:1, target:{by_content_includes:'NEEDLE'}, replacement:'SHRUNK VERSION ONE'}, {seq:2, target:{by_content_includes:'NEEDLE'}, replacement:'SHRUNK VERSION TWO'}]. 3. Run filterPipeline. 4. Observe: the toolResult content is 'SHRUNK VERSION ONE' (shrink #2 no-oped because 'NEEDLE' was removed by shrink #1). (Verified in probe2 test.)
bugs.expected: Per PRD E17: the second shrink's replacement ('SHRUNK VERSION TWO') should be what the model sees, as it was applied last in seq order.
bugs.actual: The first shrink's replacement ('SHRUNK VERSION ONE') persists because the second shrink cannot re-match the already-substituted content. No error is raised.
bugs.location: src/transforms.ts — applyShrink/resolveShrinkTarget: by_content_includes resolves against the CURRENT (possibly already-shrunk) message list, so a prior shrink changes the haystack. shrinks are applied oldest-first in filterPipeline.
bugs.suggestedFix: Document that by_content_includes is not stable across multiple shrinks on the same target (steer the agent toward by_tool_call_id/by_tool_name for multi-shrink scenarios). Alternatively, resolve all shrink targets against the ORIGINAL (pre-shrink) message list and apply substitutions by index, so each shrink independently matches the original content and last-wins by overwriting the same index.

bugs.title: Audit bloaty-flag threshold uses strict > while bloat-reminder trigger uses >= (off-by-one inconsistency at exactly the threshold)
bugs.description: The bloat-reminder nudge (nudges.ts bloatReminderHandler) fires when `bytes < threshold` is false, i.e. when bytes >= threshold (inclusive). The audit tool's bloaty flag (audit.ts renderAuditReport rows) flags a message when `messageBytes(msg) > threshold` (strict, exclusive). At exactly the threshold (e.g. 8192 bytes), a result triggers the bloat reminder but the audit does NOT flag it with the ⚠ 'above bloat threshold' marker. An agent that runs mulligan_audit after receiving a bloat reminder may see no flagged message, creating a minor inconsistency in the feedback loop the audit is meant to close.
bugs.reproduction: 1. A tool result with content whose UTF-8 byte length is exactly config.nudges.bloatThresholdBytes (8192). 2. bloatReminderHandler fires (8192 >= 8192) and appends the reminder. 3. mulligan_audit computes messageBytes = 8192 (+ reminder overhead), bloaty = 8192 > 8192 = false (before reminder overhead; with reminder overhead it flips, but the boundary semantics are inconsistent).
bugs.expected: Both the bloat reminder and the audit bloaty flag should use the same comparison (either both >= or both >), so a result that triggers a reminder is also flagged in the audit.
bugs.actual: bloatReminderHandler uses `bytes < threshold → return` (fires at >= threshold). audit bloaty uses `bytes > threshold` (flags at > threshold only). Inconsistent at the exact boundary.
bugs.location: src/nudges.ts bloatReminderHandler (`if (bytes < config.nudges.bloatThresholdBytes) return;`) vs src/tools/audit.ts (`bloaty: messageBytes(msg) > threshold`).
bugs.suggestedFix: Make both use the same operator. Recommendation: change audit's bloaty to `messageBytes(msg) >= threshold` to match the reminder trigger, or change the reminder to `bytes <= threshold → return`. Document the chosen semantics.

summary: Tested the pi-mulligan extension against the PRD via code review + adversarial filterPipeline/tool probes (the full existing suite of 697 tests already passes). The core happy-path functionality works correctly: single last_tool_call_group rewinds, default last_turn rewinds, shrink (by_tool_call_id/by_tool_name), checkpoint creation, bloat reminders, drift nudges, and audit all behave per spec. However, two MAJOR bugs were found in rewind edge cases: (1) to_previous_prompt:true is completely non-functional — the tool reports success but the filter silently no-ops because protectedOk has no to_previous_prompt exemption (spec §8 explicitly allows it); (2) checkpoint rewinds crossing the latest user partially apply (trim) instead of refusing, causing the tool to over-report the number of hidden messages and producing a non-contiguous view. Two MINOR bugs affect edge-case composition: sequential rewinds without hideEntryIds pins target each other (mitigated by the pin in normal flow), and by_content_includes shrinks don't satisfy E17's 'last wins' after substitution. One COSMETIC threshold inconsistency between the bloat reminder and audit bloaty flag was also noted. All bugs are in the rewind/shrink targeting and protection logic (transforms.ts, filter.ts, tools/rewind.ts); the pure helpers, config, markers, nudges, and audit rendering are solid.
recommendations: Fix BUG-001 first (highest impact): pass the marker's to_previous_prompt flag into protectedOk or move the latest-user check into resolveLastTurn so nuclear last_turn rewinds with 2+ users are allowed. This is the only rewind granularity that is entirely non-functional.

Fix BUG-002: make the rewind tool refuse checkpoint rewinds whose removal set crosses the latest user (mirroring step 5b), so the reported K always matches the filter's actual behavior and no partial-application non-contiguous views are created.
Fix BUG-003: collect all rewind excludeToolCallIds in filterPipeline and pass them as a set to resolveLastToolCallGroup so the live (unpinned) fallback composes correctly, not just the pin path.
Fix BUG-004: either document by_content_includes as non-stable across multi-shrink, or resolve shrink targets against the original pre-shrink message list so last-wins holds.
Align BUG-005 threshold operators (>= vs >) between bloatReminderHandler and the audit bloaty flag.

Add integration/regression tests that assert on message CONTENT/identity (not just roles) for multi-rewind composition, and add a test specifically for to_previous_prompt with 2+ user messages — the existing suite checks roles only, which masked BUG-001/BUG-003.
